title: Lantern content pack
description: A content pack for Lantern, a Shadowdark RPG companion app. DATA-MODEL.md §1 is the contract and src/model/pack.ts is that contract executable; this file is the same shape for models and editors. Every id inside a pack is written bare and namespaced by the pack id on load, so `hoarfrost` in pack `frostbound` becomes `frostbound:hoarfrost`. Nothing here is ever evaluated: `1d8` is a notation a die roller reads, never an expression.

format.description: Always "lantern-pack". It rejects unrelated JSON on the first field rather than deep inside an array.

formatVersion.description: The pack format this file is written against. Currently 1.

id.description: The pack's own id. It namespaces every id inside the pack, which is why two packs can both define a Skald without colliding.

name.description: What the content screen calls this pack.

version.description: Compared for equality only — it answers "is this the pack I already have". Semver is the convention; anything starting with a digit is accepted, so 1.2.0, 1.2.0-beta.1 and 2026.09 all pass and v1 does not.

author.description: Optional. Absent and null mean the same thing here and everywhere else in this file.

description.description: Optional. One or two sentences, shown beside the pack in the content screen.

classes.description: Optional, like every content array — a pack of four spells has one array and a pack with none at all is still a valid pack.

talents.description: Counted and not yet described. DATA-MODEL.md gives a standalone talent no shape, so the app validates nothing inside these entries and nothing reads them. Leave the array out until it has a shape.

extends.description: Additions to something another pack defined. An extension never collides; replacing something is `overrides`, which is the operation that warns.

entryId.description: An id inside this pack, written bare: `hoarfrost`, never `frostbound:hoarfrost`. The pack id is added on load.

entryRef.description: How one entry names another, in one to three segments: `dagger` in this pack, `core:dagger` with the kind implied by the field this reference sits in, or `core:item:dagger` written out in full. All three are accepted.

ref.description: The full `pack:kind:id` form and only that. Used where no field supplies the missing segments — an extension's target, and `overrides`. Kinds are class, ancestry, spell, item, talent and table.

entryName.description: Free text. One of exactly three fields that allow it — `name`, `text` and `description` — and the only one an entry must have.

entryText.description: Free text, optional everywhere it appears. Absent and null both mean "this pack does not carry the words". Nothing in this repository ships rules text; a pack a table wrote for itself may.

page.description: A page in the book this entry came from, shown when `text` is absent. Optional.

overrides.description: Replace an entry another pack defined, keeping its reference and its position in the list. This is the one operation that collides on purpose, so it warns; the last pack loaded wins.

range.description: A band, never a number of feet.

tier.description: A spell tier, 1 to 5. A number in the JSON, not a string.

die.description: A single die, as a class's hit die names one.

dieNotation.description: How a table names its dice, with an optional count in front: `2d6`, `1d20`, `d100`. No count means one die, and at most 10 dice.

damageNotation.description: What a weapon deals: one notation, or two separated by `/` for a weapon used in one hand or two. Never an expression — `1d8` and `1d4/1d8` pass, `1d8 + level/2` is refused and nothing would evaluate it if it were not.

entryTag.description: A short closed-vocabulary label, shaped like an id and deliberately not free text — `versatile`, `two-handed`. A property that needs explaining goes in `text`.

spellEntry.description: DATA-MODEL.md §3. The spell is the source of truth for which lists it is on, so adding spells to an existing class needs no extension at all.

classes.description: The classes whose lists this spell is on. A spell on no list is allowed; a picker simply never offers it.

armorBlock.description: `ac` is the class this armour sets, or the bonus a shield adds. `addDex` false is how heavy armour is expressed.

itemEntry.description: DATA-MODEL.md §4. `weapon` and `armor` are mutually exclusive in practice and not enforced to be — a shield that also hits is somebody's homebrew, not a malformed file.

slots.description: What one of it costs to carry. A sheet multiplies by quantity.

spellcastingBlock.description: Null or absent for a non-caster.

highestTierByLevel.description: Indexed by level − 1, one entry per level. A shorter list is accepted and reads as "no tier yet" past its end.

classEntry.description: DATA-MODEL.md §5. XP thresholds are uniform across classes, so there is no per-class progression to write.

weapons.description: Items this class may use. One naming an item no loaded pack defines warns and renders as plain text; it never fails the pack.

ancestryEntry.description: DATA-MODEL.md §6. The smallest entry there is.

talent.description: The words describing this ancestry's knack. Recorded, never applied — nothing in the app reads it.

tableRoll.description: A face, or an inclusive band of them: 2, or [3, 6]. `low` may equal `high`, and `low` may not exceed it — a rule this file cannot state, so the app reports it instead.

text.description: What the roll produced. A row with nothing to say is not a row. There is no `grants` field, deliberately: a result lands on a sheet as words and the app never applies it.

tableEntry.description: DATA-MODEL.md §7. Ranges must not overlap and should cover the die's whole span; a gap is a warning where the lookup happens, not a refusal here.

rerollable.description: Whether this table offers a reroll before the result is kept. Absent or null means false.

extension.description: DATA-MODEL.md §8. An extension adds two things and nothing else: talents to a class, rows to a table. There is no field that edits an entry in place and none that removes anything. An extension whose target no pack defines warns and is skipped; the pack still loads.

talents.description: Talent references to offer a class. Recorded and never resolved.

rows.description: Rows to add to a table.
